title: Alpha-beta message time
caption: Message transfer time splits into a fixed startup (protocol, queuing, FEC, software stack) and a size-over-rate term. Doubling the link rate attacks only the second term: a 4 KB handoff barely notices while a 350 MB shard halves. Collectives pay alpha once per communication round, so the fixed cost grows with participant count even on short physical paths.

symbols.meaning: fixed startup latency (~1.5 us NDR, ~5 us RoCE; effective 1-3 / 5-10 us on real stacks)
sustained link bandwidth (50 GB/s NDR, 12.5 GB/s 100G Ethernet)

title: Crossover size
caption: The message size where the transfer term equals the startup term. Below n* the link rate is nearly irrelevant: 4 KB on NDR spends ~95% of its 1.58 us in startup. Above it, bandwidth dominates: a 350 MB shard spends 99.98% in transfer. The crossover is the dividing line between buying latency and buying bandwidth.

symbols.meaning: message size where alpha equals the transfer term

title: Fat-tree host capacity
caption: A folded Clos built from k-port switches reaches k^2/2 hosts in two tiers (half each leaf's ports face down, half up) and k^3/4 in three. At radix 64 (Quantum-2 class): 2,048 and 65,536 hosts. Spending next-generation port capacity on radix instead of per-port rate is what removes a whole switching tier.

symbols.meaning: host capacity of a two-tier / three-tier fat-tree

title: Oversubscription tax
caption: When crossing traffic fills the bisection, time scales with the oversubscription ratio: a ring AllReduce with every ring edge cut runs 0.80 s on a 4:1 spine vs 0.20 s at 1:1, and 2:1 still surrenders 23.1% of throughput. At 30% of the step communicating, the book prices the 4:1 design at ~\$142.1M of waste on a \$300M cluster.

symbols.meaning: collective communication time for worst-case crossing traffic

title: Incast buffer survival
caption: A 32 MB egress buffer at 50 GB/s holds 640 us of steady backlog, but 256 synchronized senders arrive at 12.8 TB/s: the buffer overflows in under 5 us, before a congestion signal could return. Buffers buy microseconds; only scheduling and rate control buy safety.

symbols.meaning: time the egress buffer can absorb excess arrivals

title: Silent-degradation tax
caption: A single degraded link slows the synchronous step: 10% link loss becomes a 2-3% step tax after overlap. On 737,280 GPU-hours (1,024 x 30 days) that is tens of thousands of dollars, with no alarm because every dashboard reads the aggregate, not the link.

symbols.meaning: per-step slowdown from the degraded link (2-3%)
